references.text: Here Jesus confirms that his hour has come to depart from the world to the Father, which directly mirrors the statement in John 13:1 that his hour had come to leave the world and return to the Father.
Jesus proclaims that the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified, a clear parallel theme to John 13:1 where Jesus knows that his hour has come to complete his work and go to the Father.
Jesus describes his path from the Father, into the world, and back to the Father, which is the exact movement referred to in John 13:1 as going out of this world to the Father.
Jesus reminds the disciples that he is going away to the Father, a direct theme linked to John 13:1 where Jesus prepares to leave the world and return to the Father.

Here it is described that Jesus came to his own, but they did not receive him, which connects to John 13:1 where Jesus loves his own who are in the world, even though they do not always understand him.
